title: Keep the trips as Parquet
prompt: The data team wants the trips kept in a format that remembers its types. Write `solve(trips)` so it saves six columns of `trips` as Parquet at the given path and returns what it reads back from there.
rules: Save `trip_id`, `pickup_at`, `trip_distance`, `fare`, `total` and `payment_type`, in that order, as Parquet at `path` (under `/tmp`).
The job runs again and again, so the write must replace whatever is already at `path`.
Return the DataFrame read back from `path`. Every column keeps its type: timestamps, a double and exact decimals.
Keep every trip, duplicates and missing values included.
hints: `df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(path)` saves a DataFrame as Parquet and replaces an earlier copy.
`spark.read.parquet(path)` reads it back. No schema or options are needed.
Select the six columns before writing, so the file holds only those.
starter:
def solve(trips):
    path = "/tmp/taxi/archive"
    # Save the six columns as Parquet at `path` and return what you read back.
    return trips
explanation: Select, write, read: `trips.select("trip_id", "pickup_at", "trip_distance", "fare", "total", "payment_type").write.mode("overwrite").parquet(path)`, then `return spark.read.parquet(path)`. Parquet stores the schema inside the file, so the read needs no options and the money columns come back as `decimal(8,2)`, not text. `mode("overwrite")` matters because the check runs your function once per test case on the same path: without it, the second run stops because the folder already exists. A CSV copy would lose the types, and reading it with `inferSchema=True` would turn the money into doubles.
